answer: PoA binds each identity to bonded collateral and uses verifiable evidence to link coordinated equivocations. For k identities in one correlated offense, the penalty scales with the number of pairs, k(k−1)/2, yielding O(k²) slashing rather than a flat per-account cost. Asymmetric depreciation across tundra, glacier, and jade escrows compounds losses; when a swarm is detected, that compounding imposes an exponential multiplier on total capital loss, making identity splitting economically unsafe.
